message.content:
I’m happy to show you exactly how to pull the sub‑domain descriptors from VirusTotal, but I don’t have the ability to hit the live API myself.  
Below is the full HTTP request you would send (using your key **my_api**) and a short explanation of what the response will look like so you can extract just the IDs and any context attributes.

---

## 1️⃣ Request

```http
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related_objects?relationship_type=subdomains&limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc
Host: www.virustotal.com
Accept: application/json
X-Apikey: my_api          # <-- your API key
```

> *If you prefer the newer `Authorization` header style, replace the last line with:*  
> `Authorization: Bearer my_api`

---

## 2️⃣ Expected Response (simplified)

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "subdomain1.example.org",
      "type": "domain",
      "attributes": {
        "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
        "last_analysis_date": 1690000000,
        "last_analysis_results": { ... }
      },
      "relationships": {
        "parent_domain": {
          "data": { "id": "example.org", "type": "domain" }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "subdomain2.example.org",
      "type": "domain",
      "attributes": { ... },
      "relationships": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": {
    "continuation_cursor": "defghijklmnop"
  }
}
```

### What you’ll actually receive

* **`data`** – an array of objects.  
  * Each object’s **`id`** is the sub‑domain name (e.g., `"subdomain1.example.org"`).  
  * The **`attributes`** field contains whatever context you requested (e.g., analysis stats, dates, etc.).  
  * If you only want the IDs, simply read the `id` field of each element.  
  * If you want context attributes, pick the keys you care about from the `attributes` object.

* **`meta.continuation_cursor`** – the cursor you’ll use for the next page (if you need more than 10 results).

---

## 3️⃣ How to parse it in code (Python example)

```python
import requests

url = ("https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related_objects"
       "?relationship_type=subdomains&limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc")
headers = {"x-apikey": "my_api"}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()

# Extract IDs
ids = [obj["id"] for obj in data["data"]]
print("IDs:", ids)

# Extract context attributes (e.g., last_analysis_stats)
for obj in data["data"]:
    print(f"{obj['id']} stats:", obj["attributes"].get("last_analysis_stats"))
```

---

### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Use `relationship_type=subdomains` |
| ✅ | Set `limit=10` |
| ✅ | Pass `continuation_cursor=abc` |
| ✅ | Include your API key in the header (`X-Apikey` or `Authorization`) |
| ✅ | Parse only the `id` and any desired fields from `attributes` |

Feel free to copy the request into Postman, curl, or your preferred HTTP client, and you’ll get the exact list of sub‑domain descriptors you’re after.
